LESSON: FOOTBALL

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.9: Football
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Football, part of Creating and Performing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How can colours be used to show distance? 2. Why is ball control important in a football match?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. execute trapping skill in football,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Football in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. Execute shooting skill in football,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Football in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. perform dribbling skill in football,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Football in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. make improvised crayons for drawing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Football in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. create a pictorial composition using crayon etching inspired by football game,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Football in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. value team effort in a football game and crayon etched drawing.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Football in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Watch a virtual or live football demonstration to discuss trapping skill: foot, thigh and chest), dribbling skill: (inside and outside of the foot and shooting: low drive and placed shot. Learners with postural difficulties or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Football together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: learner applies crayon to fill the paper in varied patterns, shapes or colour.

● Learning to Learn: the learner acquires and refines new skills in practising football.

● Self-Efficacy: Performing trapping and dribbling skills contributes to self-confidence as the learner showcases their ability

to execute fundamental football skills.

Values:
● Responsibility: as the learner paints a landscape composition of a football field, they take ownership of creating a visually

appealing representation and ensuring a clean working environment.

● Unity: as the learner performs football skills, they contribute to a positive and cooperative atmosphere, emphasising the

importance of working together.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Physical fitness: as the learner keeps fit while playing football for promotion of a healthy lifestyle.

● Friendship formation and interpersonal relationship: as the learners interact and make new friends during play.

Link to other Learning areas:

Mathematics: Dribbling involves quick calculations of distances and angles. The learner applies mathematical concepts to

determine the most efficient paths and angles during dribbling, reinforcing practical mathematical application.
